outputs.L1:
The present invention relates to a novel process for the preparation of thieno-indole derivatives of formula (Ia) or (Ib), which employs an asymmetric synthesis to prepare key (8S)- or (8R)-8-(halomethyl)-1-alkyl-7,8-dihydro-6H-thieno[3,2-e]indol-4-ol intermediates, as well as to useful intermediate compounds in said process. Thieno-indole derivatives are described and claimed in GB2344818, WO2013/149948, and WO2013/149946, which also disclose processes for their preparation.

Enantiopure thieno-indole derivatives can now be advantageously prepared through a new asymmetric synthesis of the key 8-(halomethyl)-7,8-dihydro-6H-thieno[3,2-e]indole intermediates. By avoiding a chiral resolution step, this process provides benefits in terms of reducing the time and costs associated with the overall preparation.

The synthesis begins with the N-alkylation of 5-amino-4-halo-3-alkyl-1-benzothiophene-7-ol derivatives with enantiopure glycidyl 3-nosylate, followed by intramolecular 6-endo-tet cyclization using alkyl Grignard reagents. Mitsunobu activation of the secondary alcohol then promotes internal spirocyclization, affording the 4,4a,5,6-tetrahydro-8H-cyclopropa[c]thieno[3,2-e]indol-8-one derivatives. Finally, stereo-electronically controlled regioselective cyclopropane opening yields the key enantiopure 8-(halomethyl)-1-alkyl-7,8-dihydro-6H-thieno[3,2-e]indol-4-ol intermediates, which can be further derivatized according to the teachings disclosed in WO2013/149948 or WO2013/149946 to prepare the final thieno-indole derivatives of formula (Ia) or (Ib).

Such compounds are disclosed as alkylating compounds having cytotoxic activity and are therefore useful, as such, in the treatment of a variety of cancers and cell proliferative disorders, or, when conjugated with different types of nucleophiles, in the preparation of Antibody Drug Conjugate derivatives.

The invention concerns an improved method for producing thieno-indole compounds of formula (Ia) or (Ib). The method uses an asymmetric synthetic route to obtain the important (8S)- or (8R)-8-(halomethyl)-1-alkyl-7,8-dihydro-6H-thieno[3,2-e]indol-4-ol intermediates, and also includes intermediate compounds useful in this preparation.

Thieno-indole compounds, together with methods for making them, have previously been disclosed and claimed in GB2344818, WO2013/149948, and WO2013/149946. Enantiomerically pure thieno-indole derivatives can now be produced more efficiently by means of a new asymmetric synthesis of the key 8-(halomethyl)-7,8-dihydro-6H-thieno[3,2-e]indole intermediates. Because this approach avoids the need for a chiral resolution step, it offers advantages by shortening the process and lowering overall manufacturing costs.

The synthetic sequence begins with N-alkylation of 5-amino-4-halo-3-alkyl-1-benzothiophene-7-ol derivatives using enantiopure glycidyl 3-nosylate. This is followed by an intramolecular 6-endo-tet cyclization carried out with alkyl Grignard reagents. Activation of the resulting secondary alcohol under Mitsunobu conditions then induces an internal spirocyclization, forming 4,4a,5,6-tetrahydro-8H-cyclopropa[c]thieno[3,2-e]indol-8-one derivatives. In the final step, regioselective opening of the cyclopropane ring, governed by stereoelectronic effects, provides the key enantiopure 8-(halomethyl)-1-alkyl-7,8-dihydro-6H-thieno[3,2-e]indol-4-ol intermediates.

These intermediates may subsequently be transformed, according to the procedures described in WO2013/149948 or WO2013/149946, into the final thieno-indole compounds of formula (Ia) or (Ib). The resulting compounds are described as alkylating agents having cytotoxic properties, making them useful for treating various cancers and cell-proliferative diseases. They may also be coupled with different nucleophilic groups to produce Antibody Drug Conjugate derivatives.
outputs.L3:
The invention relates to a new process for preparing thieno-indole derivatives of formula (Ia) or (Ib) by means of asymmetric synthesis. More specifically, the process provides an efficient synthetic route to optically active thieno-indole compounds and intermediates that are useful in the preparation of biologically active alkylating agents.

A key advantage of the process is that it enables the preparation of enantiopure 8-(halomethyl)-7,8-dihydro-6H-thieno[3,2-e]indole intermediates without the need for a separate chiral resolution step. In conventional synthetic approaches, racemic mixtures often have to be separated into their individual enantiomers, which can be time-consuming, costly, and inefficient. By introducing chirality at an early stage of the synthesis through the use of enantiopure starting materials, the present process avoids this resolution step and thereby reduces both preparation time and production costs.

The synthesis begins with the N-alkylation of suitable benzothiophene derivatives using enantiopure glycidyl 3-nosylate. This reaction introduces a chiral side chain onto the nitrogen atom of the benzothiophene substrate. The resulting intermediate is then subjected to intramolecular cyclization in the presence of alkyl Grignard reagents, leading to the formation of the corresponding chiral thieno-indole framework. This step is important because it constructs the fused heterocyclic core while preserving the stereochemical information introduced by the enantiopure glycidyl reagent.

The process further involves Mitsunobu activation followed by internal spirocyclization. These transformations provide cyclopropa-thieno-indol-one derivatives, which serve as advanced intermediates in the synthetic sequence. The strained cyclopropane ring is then regioselectively opened under controlled conditions to afford the desired enantiopure 8-(halomethyl)-7,8-dihydro-6H-thieno[3,2-e]indole intermediates. The regioselectivity of this ring-opening step is significant, as it ensures formation of the desired halomethyl-substituted product in high optical purity.

The thieno-indole compounds obtained through this process possess cytotoxic alkylating activity. As a result, they may be useful as therapeutic agents, particularly in the treatment of cancer and other disorders characterized by abnormal or uncontrolled cell proliferation. In addition, these compounds or their derivatives may be employed in the preparation of antibody-drug conjugates, where their potent cytotoxic properties can be targeted selectively to diseased cells through conjugation to an antibody or other targeting moiety. Overall, the invention provides a practical and stereoselective route to valuable thieno-indole derivatives with potential applications in oncology and related therapeutic fields.
outputs.L4:
The present invention relates to improved processes for preparing enantiomerically pure thieno-indole derivatives, particularly cytotoxic thieno-indole compounds and intermediates useful in their manufacture. More specifically, the invention provides a new asymmetric synthetic route to key chiral intermediates of formula (8S) or (8R) 8-(halomethyl)-1-alkyl-7,8-dihydro-6H-thieno[3,2-e]indol-4-ol. These intermediates are valuable building blocks for the synthesis of biologically active thieno-indole compounds, including compounds suitable for use as anti-cancer agents and as payloads in antibody-drug conjugates.

The process described herein avoids the need for classical chiral resolution of racemic material. Instead, chirality is introduced and controlled during the synthesis, allowing direct access to the desired enantiomer in high optical purity. This represents a significant improvement over prior methods, which often require the preparation of racemic intermediates followed by resolution using chiral acids, chiral chromatography, enzymatic methods, or other separation techniques. Such resolution procedures can be time-consuming, expensive, inefficient, and difficult to scale, especially when only one enantiomer is therapeutically useful.

In one aspect, the invention provides an asymmetric synthesis involving a sequence of key transformations. The route begins with N-alkylation of an appropriate thieno-indole precursor to introduce the desired alkyl substituent at the nitrogen atom. The resulting intermediate is then subjected to a Grignard-mediated cyclization step, which constructs an important cyclic framework required for formation of the thieno[3,2-e]indole core. Subsequent Mitsunobu-promoted spirocyclization generates a strained spirocyclopropane intermediate in a stereochemically controlled manner. Finally, regioselective opening of the cyclopropane ring affords the desired chiral 8-(halomethyl)-substituted 7,8-dihydro-6H-thieno[3,2-e]indol-4-ol intermediate.

The stereochemical outcome of the synthesis may be controlled to provide either the (8S) or the (8R) enantiomer, depending on the choice of chiral starting material, reagent, or reaction conditions. The halomethyl group at the 8-position may include, for example, chloromethyl, bromomethyl, or iodomethyl substituents, each of which may serve as a functional handle for further chemical elaboration. The 1-alkyl group may be selected according to the desired final thieno-indole compound and may include lower alkyl substituents or other alkyl groups compatible with the reaction sequence.

The chiral intermediates prepared by this method can be converted into a variety of thieno-indole derivatives having potent cytotoxic activity. Such compounds are useful in the treatment of cancer and other diseases associated with abnormal or excessive cell proliferation. In addition, because of their high potency, these compounds may be especially useful as drug payloads in targeted therapeutic constructs, such as antibody-drug conjugates. In such conjugates, the cytotoxic thieno-indole compound may be linked to an antibody or antigen-binding fragment through a suitable linker, enabling selective delivery of the cytotoxic agent to cells expressing a target antigen.

The invention therefore provides both synthetic and practical advantages. By eliminating chiral resolution, the process reduces the number of manufacturing steps, improves material efficiency, lowers production costs, and shortens overall processing time. The route is also well suited for scale-up because it relies on robust chemical transformations and provides direct access to enantiopure intermediates. These benefits make the process particularly valuable for the industrial preparation of thieno-indole-based therapeutic agents.

Accordingly, the invention encompasses methods for preparing enantiopure 8-(halomethyl)-1-alkyl-7,8-dihydro-6H-thieno[3,2-e]indol-4-ol intermediates, the intermediates obtained by such methods, and their use in preparing cytotoxic thieno-indole compounds. The invention further relates to pharmaceutical compounds derived from these intermediates, pharmaceutical compositions comprising such compounds, methods of treating cancer or proliferative diseases using such compounds, and antibody-drug conjugates incorporating thieno-indole cytotoxic payloads produced through the described asymmetric synthetic approach.
outputs.L5:
**The Thieno Grignard Reaction: A Useful Tool in Organic Synthesis**

The **Thieno Grignard** reaction refers to the use of Grignard reagents containing a **thieno** or thiophene-based structure in organic synthesis. Thiophene is a five-membered aromatic ring containing sulfur, and compounds built from this ring are important in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and advanced materials.

A Grignard reagent is typically formed when an organic halide reacts with magnesium metal in dry ether or tetrahydrofuran. In the case of a thieno Grignard reagent, a halogenated thiophene derivative can be converted into an organomagnesium compound. This reagent is highly reactive and can form new carbon–carbon bonds, making it valuable for building more complex molecules.

The main advantage of using thieno Grignard reagents is their ability to introduce thiophene-containing groups into aldehydes, ketones, esters, and other electrophiles. For example, reaction with an aldehyde or ketone can produce an alcohol bearing a thieno substituent. These products may later be modified further to create biologically active compounds or functional organic materials.

Because Grignard reagents are sensitive to moisture and air, the reaction must be carried out under anhydrous conditions. Even small amounts of water can destroy the reagent and reduce the yield. Despite this limitation, the Thieno Grignard approach remains an important method in synthetic chemistry.

In summary, **the Thieno Grignard** reaction combines the reactivity of Grignard chemistry with the usefulness of thiophene-based structures. It provides an efficient way to create carbon–carbon bonds and synthesize compounds with potential applications in medicine, materials science, and chemical research.

counterfactuals.output:
## Patent-Style Summary

The present invention relates to improved processes for the asymmetric synthesis of enantiomerically enriched or enantiopure thieno-indole derivatives, and in particular to methods employing chiral 8-(halomethyl)-7,8-dihydro-6H-thieno[3,2-e]indole intermediates as key synthetic building blocks. The invention further relates to such intermediates, compositions comprising them, and their use in the preparation of pharmaceutically active compounds and analogues thereof.

Thieno-indole compounds and related tricyclic heteroaromatic systems have been described as useful intermediates or active pharmaceutical entities. Prior disclosures include, for example, GB2344818, which describes thieno-indole derivatives and associated synthetic approaches, and WO2013/149948 and WO2013/149946, which disclose further thieno-indole-based compounds and methods relevant to their preparation and therapeutic use. However, known synthetic routes may involve racemic intermediates, resolution steps, limited stereochemical control, or process conditions that are less suitable for efficient preparation of single-enantiomer products on scale.

In one aspect, the invention provides an asymmetric process for preparing an enantiopure thieno-indole derivative, the process comprising forming or providing an enantioenriched 8-(halomethyl)-7,8-dihydro-6H-thieno[3,2-e]indole intermediate of Formula I:

**Formula I:**  
8-(CH₂X)-7,8-dihydro-6H-thieno[3,2-e]indole,

wherein X is a halogen selected from chloro, bromo, or iodo, preferably chloro or bromo, and wherein the stereogenic center at the 8-position is present in a predetermined absolute configuration and in high enantiomeric excess.

In certain embodiments, the intermediate of Formula I is prepared by an asymmetric reduction, asymmetric hydrogenation, chiral auxiliary-mediated transformation, enzymatic resolution, catalytic enantioselective cyclization, or stereospecific functional group conversion of a corresponding prochiral or enantioenriched precursor. In preferred embodiments, the process provides the 8-(halomethyl)-7,8-dihydro-6H-thieno[3,2-e]indole intermediate in an enantiomeric excess of at least 90%, preferably at least 95%, more preferably at least 98%, and most preferably at least 99%.

In another aspect, the invention provides a stereospecific conversion of the enantiopure 8-(halomethyl) intermediate into a substituted thieno-indole derivative by displacement of the halomethyl group with a nucleophile. Suitable nucleophiles include, without limitation, amines, alcohols, thiols, azides, cyanide equivalents, organometallic reagents, and heteroatom-containing pharmaceutical side-chain precursors. The substitution may proceed with retention or inversion of configuration depending on the reaction mechanism and conditions selected, thereby allowing controlled access to either enantiomer of the desired thieno-indole product.

In selected embodiments, the halomethyl intermediate is converted to compounds corresponding to, or useful in preparing compounds disclosed in, GB2344818, WO2013/149948, or WO2013/149946. The present process may therefore provide an improved route to known biologically active thieno-indole derivatives, including single-enantiomer forms thereof, while reducing or avoiding chromatographic resolution, improving overall yield, enhancing stereochemical purity, and facilitating scale-up.

The invention also encompasses salts, solvates, protected forms, and crystalline forms of the intermediates and products described herein. In some embodiments, the thieno-indole derivative prepared according to the invention is isolated as a pharmaceutically acceptable salt. In further embodiments, the process includes purification by crystallization, salt formation, chiral salt enrichment, or selective precipitation to afford material suitable for pharmaceutical manufacture.

A further aspect of the invention provides an industrially applicable process comprising:  
1. preparing a chiral precursor to a 7,8-dihydro-6H-thieno[3,2-e]indole core;  
2. introducing a halomethyl substituent at the 8-position to form an enantioenriched 8-(halomethyl)-7,8-dihydro-6H-thieno[3,2-e]indole; and  
3. converting said halomethyl substituent into a desired side chain to obtain an enantiopure thieno-indole derivative.

The process is advantageous in that the stereochemical information is established before late-stage functionalization, permitting divergent synthesis of multiple analogues from a common enantiopure intermediate. This approach provides improved flexibility relative to routes requiring separate asymmetric synthesis or resolution of each final compound.

In particular embodiments, the invention provides an asymmetric synthesis of compounds structurally related to those disclosed in GB2344818, WO2013/149948, and WO2013/149946, wherein the use of an enantiopure 8-(halomethyl)-7,8-dihydro-6H-thieno[3,2-e]indole intermediate enables efficient preparation of single-enantiomer thieno-indole derivatives in high chemical purity and high enantiomeric purity.

Accordingly, the invention provides novel and improved methods for producing enantiopure thieno-indole derivatives, key chiral halomethyl intermediates useful therein, and downstream products obtainable by such methods.

counterfactuals.prompt: In patent language, summarize a synthetic route starting from N-alkylation of 5-amino-4-halo-3-alkyl-1-benzothiophene-7-ol with enantiopure glycidyl nosylate, Grignard-mediated cyclization, Mitsunobu spirocyclization, and regioselective cyclopropane opening to make thieno-indoles.
counterfactuals.output:
In one embodiment, thieno-indole compounds, including enantioenriched spirocyclic thieno-indole derivatives, are prepared by a process comprising the following sequence of transformations.

A substituted 5-amino-4-halo-3-alkyl-1-benzothiophene-7-ol is first subjected to chemoselective N-alkylation with an enantiomerically enriched glycidyl nosylate under basic conditions to provide the corresponding N-glycidylated benzothiophene intermediate. The use of the enantiopure epoxide electrophile establishes the absolute configuration of the side chain and provides an optically enriched precursor suitable for subsequent ring-forming operations.

The N-glycidylated intermediate is then treated with an organomagnesium reagent under conditions effective to promote metal–halogen exchange or Grignard formation at the 4-halo position, followed by intramolecular cyclization onto the pendant epoxide. This transformation furnishes a fused thieno-indoline or thieno-indole alcohol intermediate in which the newly formed carbon–carbon bond constructs the core bicyclic heteroaromatic framework.

The resulting alcohol is thereafter converted to a spirocyclic intermediate by an intramolecular Mitsunobu reaction. In particular, activation of the hydroxy group in the presence of a phosphine and an azodicarboxylate reagent promotes cyclodehydrative displacement by a suitably positioned phenolic or heteroatom nucleophile, thereby providing a spirocyclic thieno-indole compound with inversion at the reacting stereocenter where applicable.

In a further embodiment, the spirocyclic intermediate comprises a fused or pendant cyclopropane moiety. Regioselective opening of said cyclopropane is effected under nucleophilic, Lewis acidic, protic, or otherwise activating conditions to afford ring-opened thieno-indole products. Selection of the opening reagent and reaction conditions provides control over the site of bond cleavage and the identity of the substituent introduced, thereby furnishing a series of functionalized thieno-indole derivatives.

Accordingly, the route provides a stereochemically defined synthesis of thieno-indoles from readily substituted 5-amino-4-halo-3-alkyl-1-benzothiophene-7-ol precursors through sequential N-alkylation with an enantiopure glycidyl nosylate, Grignard-mediated intramolecular cyclization, Mitsunobu spirocyclization, and regioselective cyclopropane ring opening.

counterfactuals.prompt: Compose the “field and background of the invention” section for a patent application claiming a new asymmetric process for thieno-indole enantiomers useful as anticancer compounds and antibody-drug conjugate payloads.
counterfactuals.output:
## FIELD OF THE INVENTION

The present invention relates generally to synthetic organic chemistry and medicinal chemistry. More particularly, the invention relates to asymmetric processes for preparing enantioenriched thieno-indole compounds, including thieno-indole enantiomers and pharmaceutically acceptable salts, solvates, stereoisomeric forms, and intermediates thereof. The thieno-indole compounds prepared by the processes described herein are useful as biologically active agents, including anticancer agents, and as payloads, payload precursors, or payload-linker constructs for targeted drug delivery systems such as antibody-drug conjugates.

## BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

Cancer remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, and there is a continuing need for new therapeutic agents having improved potency, selectivity, pharmacokinetic properties, and tolerability. Small-molecule cytotoxic agents continue to play an important role in oncology therapy, both as stand-alone chemotherapeutic agents and as components of targeted delivery platforms. In particular, antibody-drug conjugates (“ADCs”) have emerged as an important class of therapeutics that combine the targeting ability of an antibody or other binding moiety with the cytotoxic activity of a drug payload. In an ADC, the payload is typically attached to the targeting moiety through a linker designed to provide adequate stability in circulation while permitting release of the active drug at or near a target cell.

The development of ADCs has increased the demand for highly potent payloads that can be manufactured reproducibly and with well-defined chemical and stereochemical purity. Payloads suitable for ADC applications often possess complex structures and may include one or more stereogenic elements. Because the biological activity, toxicity, stability, linker compatibility, and pharmacological properties of such compounds can vary significantly depending on stereochemistry, the ability to access a desired enantiomer in high enantiomeric excess is of substantial importance.

Thieno-indole compounds represent a class of heteroaromatic molecules of interest in drug discovery. Certain thieno-indole derivatives exhibit biological activity relevant to cancer treatment, including cytotoxic, antiproliferative, or other antitumor effects. Thieno-indole frameworks may also provide useful structural features for incorporation into potent payloads for targeted drug delivery systems, including ADCs. However, the preparation of stereochemically defined thieno-indole compounds can be challenging, particularly where the desired molecule contains a stereogenic center or axis formed during construction or functionalization of the thieno-indole core.

Conventional methods for preparing chiral thieno-indole compounds may rely on non-stereoselective synthesis followed by separation of enantiomers, for example by chiral chromatography or resolution using a chiral resolving agent. Such approaches can be inefficient, costly, and difficult to scale, particularly where the undesired enantiomer is discarded or where chromatographic separation is required at a late stage of synthesis. Other approaches may employ chiral starting materials or auxiliaries, but these methods can require additional synthetic steps, generate stoichiometric waste, or be limited in substrate scope. In addition, known routes may provide insufficient enantioselectivity, poor chemical yield, undesirable impurity profiles, or conditions that are incompatible with sensitive functional groups used for subsequent linker attachment or payload derivatization.

For pharmaceutical and ADC applications, there is also a need for synthetic processes that are robust, scalable, and capable of delivering the desired thieno-indole enantiomer with high chemical purity and high enantiomeric purity. Such processes should preferably avoid or reduce the need for preparative chiral separation, provide access to either enantiomer when desired, and be compatible with functionalized intermediates suitable for conversion into drug payloads, linker-payloads, or conjugatable derivatives.

Accordingly, there remains a need in the art for improved asymmetric processes for preparing thieno-indole enantiomers, including processes that provide high yield, high enantioselectivity, operational simplicity, and suitability for manufacture. The present invention addresses these and other needs by providing asymmetric methods for the synthesis of enantioenriched thieno-indole compounds useful as anticancer compounds and as payloads or payload intermediates for antibody-drug conjugates.
